question_text: PPL is a professional sports league based in India, which is currently in its second season. In the league stage of the competition, six teams compete in 10 different categories (6 for men, 3 for women, and 1 for specially-abled) before 4 teams qualify for the playoffs. Parvin Dabas, the actor from Khosla ka Ghosla and Monsoon Wedding, is a co-founder and key promoter of the league. In 2023, Suniel Shetty came onboard as a minority stakeholder of the league. What sport that is considered a display of physical dominance, strength, and toughness, is played in this league?

On June 14, 2020,  social media users started an unofficial trend, and began celebrating X Day. Users posted pictures of X, often accompanied with the hashtag #AllBirthdaysMatter.
The trend resurfaced again on June 14, 2025. The reason for the date was simple - June 14 is Y's birthday.
ID X and Y.

In 1976, the CBI arrested X, among others, in what was called the Baroda Dynamite Case. The accused were charged of smuggling dynamite to blow up government establishments and railway tracks in protest against the state of emergency. They were also charged with waging war against the state to overthrow the government. The case was tried in Delhi, as the CBI argued that even though the site of the incident was Baroda, the case had national ramifications. All the accused were, thus,  imprisoned in Tihar Jail, Delhi. The case was withdrawn when Janata Party came to power in 1977. ID X, the most prominent accused in the case.

X is a Young Adult Romance Novel by Wendy Brant. The story is about 17-yr old Eva Walker, a math genius with a paranormal gift - she can read people's secrets, insecurities, and fears when she touches them or their personal articles. To avoid any unnecessary drama, she lives like a loner, and keeps her hands to herself. Until she meets six-foot-three, cute-without-trying Zenn Bennett, who makes that nearly impossible. What is the title of this book, that is a wordplay on something you may see in memes, or elementary set theory?

In 1967, K.V. Switzer did something unprecedented, becoming the first to accomplish something. Before Switzer, B. Gibb did do the same thing an year prior, but it wasn't officially recognized or sanctioned. Switzer's attempt was not without hurdles, either. Jock Semple, the person who had organized the "event",  tried to tackle and stop Switzer from participating, but was prevented from doing so by friends of Switzer.
What did Switzer finally accomplish?
answer_text: First Woman to Complete Boston Marathon

question_text: X is a Mexican brand of Indoor Theme Parks, with franchises in multiple countries around the world - including UK, Japan, Kuwait, Philippines, and India, among others. In India, the franchise is held by Imagination Edutainment Pvt Ltd, in which Shah Rukh Khan owns a 26% stake. In June earlier this year, X was trending on social media with users pointing out how a certain feature of the theme park bore an uncanny similarity with the Air India crash. Air India is one of the brand partners of X India. ID X.

X was a viral Internet video trend which became popular in November 2016. The videos in this trend, shot with a moving camera, were often accompanied by the song "Black Beatles" by Rae Sremmurd playing in the background. The trend was started by students at a high school in Jacksonville, Florida. The initial posting inspired works by other groups, especially professional athletes and sports teams, who posted increasingly complex and elaborate videos. News outlets compared the videos to bullet time scenes from science fiction films such as The Matrix and the X-Men movies featuring Quicksilver. ID this trend.

X was a political party in India which had its roots in the All-India Scheduled Castes Federation. The formation of the party was announced by B.R. Ambedkar, shortly before his death. In 1957, six members of the party were elected to the second Lok Sabha. That number was never breached in its history. Following internal strife, the party broke up into more than 50 factions. Today, the only off-shoot recognized by the ECI is X (Athawale) led by Ramdas Athawale. In 2014, Rakhi Sawant joined this party. ID X.

X was an Indian playback singer, sometimes referred to as 'The Vibrant Voice of India'. X was the first Indian playback singer to record music in English. He also recorded a pop album titled 'M-3' which had Boney M songs translated in Hindi.
Over his career, X came to be known as the voice of Manoj Kumar since he lent his voice to many of his films. Also known for singing in multiple other languages, in Marathi cinema he became popular for being the voice of Dada Kondke in his movies.
ID this versatile singer X.

X was an American writer whose novels have sold over 300 million copies in 51 languages. He is consistently cited as one of the top 10 best-selling fiction writers of all time. His novel writing began after he turned 50. Before that X was a prominent writer for Broadway, Films, and TV. He won an Oscar in 1948 for Best Screenplay, and created hit shows like the Patty Duke Show, and I Dream of Jeanie. His remarkable life is encapsulated in his autobiography, The Other Side of Me, a play on his novel, The Other Side of Midnight, which has also been adapted into a Hindi movie, Oh Bewafa! ID X.

The Altamont Speedway Free Festival was a counterculture rock concert in the United States, held four months after Woodstock. The festival was dubbed "Woodstock West" and was expected to follow the success of the earlier festival. Unfortunately, the event was marred by significant violence, three accidental deaths, and one stabbing. This despite X being hired as security for the event, in exchange for beer, something that X regularly did at rock shows. Who or what is/are X?

X is an American singer and actor, with a much more famous daughter. For the longest time, X's only claim to fame was a hit single 'Achy breaky heart' from 1992. In 2001, X appeared in a film directed by Y, an American filmmaker known for his experimental style. Strangely enough, decades after this appearance, X began crediting Y for his daughter's success too, stating that ________ ________, a TV show that made his daughter famous, wouldn't have happened if not for the opportunity presented by Y to him. These interviews resurfaced after Y's demise earlier this year, putting fresh light on this nepo father. ID X and Y.

In 2018, X, a clothing brand, found itself at the center of a social media firestorm after posting an image of child model Liam Mango, a five-year old Black child, modeling a hoodie with the words "Coolest Monkey in the Jungle." While the brand likely intended the hoodie to be playful, the ad was seen by many as racially insensitive. Social media users quickly pointed out the problematic nature of the phrase, particularly given the historical use of "monkey" as a racial slur. ID the brand X.

The word X originates from an obsolete English verb which means 'to fart'. It was used to describe a weak or ineffective sound, akin to a hissing or sputtering noise.
The term has evolved to refer to a failure or abortive effort, often implying a weak or disappointing outcome, such as a project that ends abruptly or a performance that fails to meet expectations.
ID the word X.

The meaning and connotation of the word X, today, is completely different from how it was originally used in the 16th century. X used to be a term of endearment, akin to sweetheart, and was used for either sexes. Consider this from Henry V by William Shakespeare, written in 1600: "I kiss his dirty shoe, and from heart-string I love the lovely X. What is thy name?"
The word today has a negative connotation, and is also the title of a single-player action-adventure video game, published by Rockstar Games in 2006. ID X.

X is a 1969 Indian fantasy adventure comedy film, written and directed by Y, based on a story by his grandfather. One of the reasons behind the making of X was that Y's son wanted him to make a film which was less 'grim and adult'. X thought this would also give him an opportunity to lace the story with music and dancing, a point his movies' producers and distributors were always insisting upon. There are two sequels to the film, the first of which was released in 1980, again written and directed by Y.  The third film in the series was written by Y, but directed by his son, and was released in 1992. ID X and Y.
answer_text: Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne; Satyajit Ray
